To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) NLO corrections to ZZ + jet are large, but the NLO predictions are under control and the K-factor is well-behaved, (b) NLO corrections for the graviton plus jet process are very large and the K-factor exhibits large logarithmic terms that spoil the convergence of the perturbative expansion, and that (c) these large logarithms can be absorbed into a redefinition of the parton distribution functions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of multi-particle scattering processes with a large number of particles in the final state.
precision calculations in quantum field theory.
the computation of NLO QCD corrections in the context of precision physics at hadron collider.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NLO QCD predictions for ZZ jet production and graviton jet production are under control, and can be used for precision studies at LHC.
the GOLEM approach to the tensor reduction is a very efficient tool in obtaining precise predictions for hadronic collisions at next-to-leading order.
the NLO QCD corrections are important and should be included in the analysis of all these processes, in order to obtain precise predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GOLEM methods have been applied to a number of processes at hadron collides, which are of importance for the LHC physics.
the GOLEM methods are very useful for NLO calculations in the context of hadron collider physics.
the NLO corrections are large, but the NLO predictions are stable and well behaved.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the tensor reduction using GOLEMs is a powerful tool for obtaining NLO QCD results for processes with one or more massive particles, which are relevant for Higgs and beyond the standard model physics searches.
the tensor reduction of one-loop integrals using GOLEM methods is an efficient way for precise NLO calculations.
, in spite of the complexity of the tensor integrals involved, the NLO corrections can be calculated with reasonable resources and are of the same order of magnitude as the leading order (LO) result.
